newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungarian shares drift lower, but above day's.
newsitem.headline: Hungarian shares drift lower, but above day's.

text.p: Hungarian share prices drifted lower on Thursday after three sessions of bull run, but fresh buyings at lower level helped prices in recovering from the day's lows.
The BUX index finished at a preliminary 6,731.57 points, downn 48.02 points, but well above the day's low of 6,640.28.

"The pattern of the move clearly pointed to just some general profit-taking especially across those shares which have been recently quite strong," said Roger Monson, Chief Equity Strategist at Daiwa Europe in London.
"That is fairly healthy, I think," he added.
Traders said earlier during the session that share prices were trimmed also by position closings on the futures market as investors sold stocks on the cash market.
"Price falls on the futures market showed that these were tactics of investors closing hedge deals," added Tamas Petheo of Buda-Cash Brokerhaz.
On Thursday, actively traded retailer Fotex bucked the trend and closed more than 14 percent higher, at 174 forints, up 22, on strong buys by one brokerage.
High-caps, oil firm MOL, chemicals TVK and BorsodChem, all jumped to new record levels before retreating to close lower.
MOL ended at 4,255 forints, down 80. It announced this morning that it would invest 49 billion forints on a residue upgrading project and a hydrogen plant at its Duna refinery.
Analysts said the fact that the market recovered from the day's lows was a positive sign and gains might come on Friday.

"I like the way the market has moved, it had some sellings down to 6,640 (points) and you immediately had buying coming in at a reasonably high level...and so now it's back up to a modest loss of less than one percent," Daiwa's Monson said.
"I would imagine that tomorrow's trading will continue this renewed buying and probably finish at another record, barring a major external influence."
